(The original text is written in Draconic and appears to be an introduction to an ancient capital.)
Those who visit this land for the first time often see the gate before they see the city itself. Rising between the slopes and waterways, that gate stands tall enough to overlook a hundred districts, its silhouette visible even from across distant rivers. Thus, travelers arriving from the south lay eyes upon their destination long before entering the city.
Looking down from the city's heights, the inner citadel where the Dragonkin dwell stretches out in orderly tiers. Looking up from below, stone stairs, galleries, and dwellings rise in layers, as though every current converges toward a single center. Though countless souls live here, what first captivates the eye is neither the houses nor the bustle of the markets, but the Divine Gate. It is at once a colossal monument standing within the city and a crown adorning the whole.
The Dragonkin reside near the Divine Gate, governing the laws and affairs of state. Humans dwell across the outer districts, plying myriad trades to form the markets. Beastkin move to and fro between them, each taking up transport and labor. The greatness of this city lies not only in the expanse of its walls, but in how its many races live together while preserving order.
Yet the true majesty of this city resides less in the size of its populace than in an unspoken order that makes itself felt. Visitors naturally lower their voices without anyone bidding them to do so. Therefore, I set down this single note:
What makes this city worthy of record is not its prosperity alone, but that a traveler from afar knows at a single glance that this is no ordinary city.

[Special Feature] Visiting Fleece During the Golden Wheat Carnival
By Orman Pancook
As you may know, the Golden Wheat Carnival is a trade festival held in Fleece every two lunar cycles. During this time, merchant guilds from Fleece, the Chen Dynasty, the Rosia Empire, Avarian, and beyond bring their finest goods to Fleece to display and sell throughout the Golden Wheat Carnival.
The history of the Golden Wheat Carnival stretches far back into the past.
According to tradition, when the ancestors of the people of Fleece first arrived here, it was still a nameless wilderness wedged between three nations. Alongside the Kibo with whom they had formed Starlinks, they tamed this land through their steadfast character and diligent labor, gradually building wealth by trading their harvests with neighboring nations and transforming this small territory into a hub of commerce spanning not only the three nations, but far beyond.
Today, the residents of Fleece no longer worry over basic necessities like food, clothing, and shelter; instead, as hosts of this open and welcoming city, they greet merchant guilds and travelers from all across the continent. Moreover, to honor the wisdom and diligence of their forebears, the people of Fleece established a day during the harvest season as the Golden Wheat Carnival. The festival is not merely a memorial to their ancestors, but also a symbol of yearning and hope for a prosperous, joyful life. The sight of golden wheat swaying in the breeze seems to tell the very story of Fleece, irresistibly drawing visitors into the charm of this land. Over time, the Golden Wheat Carnival has become a vital part of Fleece's culture, and countless tourists visit Fleece to experience the festivities firsthand.
If you visit Fleece during the Golden Wheat Carnival, the "Special Auction" is an event you simply cannot miss.
Grandly hosted by the lord on the final day of the carnival, the Special Auction is the festival's climax and its most thrilling spectacle. Merchant guilds from every nation and independent trading companies spare no effort in preparing their finest wares for this occasion. The items carefully selected by merchants are registered in advance to await the bidding.
Once the preview period begins, the registered items become the center of everyone's attention. Visitors eagerly inspect the exhibits, thoroughly researching their quality, historical background, and more. Buyers and interested onlookers are free to browse the items and decide whether to take part in the auction. This stage gives people a chance to compare and evaluate the goods while also serving as a crucial step for participants to plan their bidding strategies.
During the Special Auction itself, the registered items are brought out one by one onto the auction block. An intense and electrifying bidding war ensues as buyers compete to claim the treasures they desire. The auctioneer's brisk gestures, impassioned calls for higher bids, and ever-climbing prices create a thrilling scene brimming with excitement. Every single bid has the potential to turn the tide of the entire auction, and participants strive to claim victory in this contest of wit and nerve.
Throughout the entire auction, the venue buzzes with tension and fervor as the crowd watches every step with rapt attention. The lord oversees the proceedings with an impartial hand to ensure fairness. Once the auction concludes, successful bidders head home satisfied, while even those who walked away empty-handed gain valuable insight from the experience.
Concluding the festivities, the Special Auction is not merely the climax of the carnival, but also a stage for every participant to showcase their skill and acumen.

Different waters hold different fish, and your fishing technique must change accordingly. Choosing the right method for the terrain can greatly increase your catch. Basic fishing techniques include:

These techniques are primarily suited to freshwater fishing. Adapting them to the situation can greatly boost your catch rate.

1518767:
[The Tale of the Three Kibo]
Deep in a distant forest lived three adorable Kibo: Foundy, Screin, and Grumank. These three Kibo were the guardians of the land, each possessing their own special wisdom and strength.
Foundy had a gentle nature and was a friend to every Kibo in the forest. Screin was thrifty and clever, always gathering food while building the coziest nest imaginable. Grumank boasted tremendous strength, protecting weaker companions and giving everyone peace of mind.
One day, a powerful Kibo suddenly arrived in the forest and made a loud proclamation: "I shall build a kingdom in this forest, and all Kibo shall live within it! This kingdom will be a land of 99 steps. The Kibo on the 99th step will clean and sweep, the Kibo on the 63rd step will tend the fires, and the Kibo on the 24th step will paint portraits. And I shall sit upon a feather quilt on the 1st step, gazing out over my ever-prospering realm."
Hearing this, the forest Kibo grew anxious and turned to Foundy, Screin, and Grumank for help. The three Kibo gathered together and held a strategy meeting.
Screin gave his tail a brisk wag and said, "Let's reinforce our nests so everyone has a safe place to live."
Grumank beat his chest and declared, "With this strength of mine, I'll protect every last Kibo!"
Foundy blinked thoughtfully and proposed a plan: "First, let's observe this uninvited guest and see whether they will truly bring prosperity to our land."
After a period of watching and testing the waters, the three Kibo came to a realization. Though this outsider Kibo possessed both power and ambition, they also harbored a desire to be respected and accepted. Thus, the three decided to give the newcomer a chance to become part of their community. Foundy spoke to the outsider: "You may live here, provided you follow our rules—so that all Kibo may live freely and happily."
Upon hearing this, the outsider Kibo pondered for a long while before finally accepting the offer. The outsider promised to abide by their rules and live in peace alongside the other Kibo.
And so, a kingdom was born in the forest—not a kingdom belonging to any single Kibo, but one without rank or hierarchy, where every Kibo gladly offered their strength for the good of the land. Thanks to everyone working together to protect their beautiful forest, the land prospered more than ever and became a truly wonderful place.
1518768:
[The Tale of Melo]
In a faraway land lived a Meloomy named Melo. Known for pure white fur and big, bright eyes, Melo was always brimming with curiosity about the world around them.
However, Melo had one small problem. Whenever a strong wind blew through the forest, Melo would get frightened, hide inside a tree hollow, and refuse to come out.
One day, a fierce wind suddenly swept through the forest, bending branches and sending leaves swirling through the air. Terrified, Melo squeezed their eyes shut and curled up inside the hollow, thinking, "What a fierce wind... At this rate, my whole nest might get blown away!"
Just then, a rhythmic knocking sounded at the door. "Melo, Melo, let's go for a walk in the forest together!" It was Melo's friend Nyanya the Melareed, come to invite Melo out to play.
Truth be told, Melo wanted to go too, yet the howling wind outside was simply too frightening. Huddling deeper into the nest, Melo called back through the door, "B-but the wind is so strong out there. Maybe next time..."
Nyanya shook her head and waddled away.
A little while later, another knock echoed at the door. Soon, a cheerful voice drifted in from outside—it was Melo's friend Puppu the Mokyun. "Melo, come out with us! Today's a wonderful day for an outing!"
Melo repeated the exact same answer given to Nyanya earlier. To that, Puppu replied, "Even I'm a Mokyun, and I'm not worried about being blown away by the wind! What are you so afraid of?" Still, those words weren't enough to ease Melo's fears, and Puppu reluctantly headed off alone.
Melo stayed cooped up inside the tree hollow all alone. It was a little boring, but at least there was no worry of getting swept away by the wind. The afternoon passed, and as evening drew near, the sound of the wind finally died down. Hopping and skipping, Melo emerged from the tree hollow and headed toward where the two friends were waiting in the forest.
Yet just as Melo spotted them in the distance, the wind began to blow once more. Startled, Melo started to turn back toward the hollow when Puppu shouted loudly from behind, "Melo, look over there!"
Following where Puppu pointed, Melo saw a flock of Windels—the forest wind had been their mischievous prank all along!
Relieved, Melo stopped in their tracks. Nyanya and Puppu hurried over to Melo's side, and the three little friends played joyfully together for a long time, happier than could be.
Melo especially played harder and more freely than ever before, realizing for the very first time that the thing they had feared for so long wasn't really so scary after all.
1518769:
[Eileen's Magic Hoe]
On the outskirts of a quiet, remote village lay fields that appeared ordinary at first glance, yet pulsed with vitality. Tucked away in one corner of those fields sat a plain-looking hoe. Its surface was caked in dirt and moss, though whenever the moonlight fell upon it, a faint shimmer could be seen gliding across the blade.
Eileen was an ordinary resident of the village and a young farmer. Kindhearted and hardworking, she was nevertheless at her wits' end over the fields before her. The Brocade Moon was fast approaching, yet her hoe had broken during yesterday's labor. There wasn't enough time to have a new one forged, and all her neighbors were busy preparing for the coming planting season, leaving no spare hoes for Eileen to borrow.
As she walked along the edge of her field trying to think of a solution, her foot struck something hard. Crouching down, she discovered it was a hoe. Eileen's heart leapt with joy—until she looked closer and saw how old and worn it was. Thinking it looked completely unusable, her spirits sank.
Still, with nothing else to work with, she had no other choice. Reluctantly, she decided to give it a try. The moment she swung it, Eileen gasped in astonishment. This was no ordinary hoe. Not only could it till the earth before her with astonishing speed, but with every swing, clear spring water welled up to nourish the long-parched soil. Unbeknownst to her, it was a legendary magic hoe gifted with the wondrous power to turn barren ground into fertile soil in the blink of an eye.
Filled with renewed hope, Eileen threw herself into tilling the land. In mere moments, she had finished several days' worth of labor. Making no secret of the magic hoe, she generously lent it out to her fellow villagers as well. Before long, the entire village's fields were tilled far sooner than usual.
Soon after, the villagers realized the magic hoe held an even greater marvel—it could accelerate crop growth and increase yields as well. For a time, Eileen became the center of the village, with everyone flocking to borrow the magic hoe. Thanks to its power, the villagers finished their farmwork swiftly and soon celebrated a bountiful harvest. As they tilled and planted more and more frequently, the land yielded one rich harvest after another.
Gradually, however, everyone noticed the magic hoe's effects beginning to fade. While it could still till the soil effortlessly, crop yields dropped back to what they had been before the hoe was found—and soon fell even lower. Some even began to suspect that Eileen had secretly tampered with the hoe. Yet once they saw that Eileen's own fields were suffering the exact same fate, no one could say a word.
Eileen herself was deeply troubled. Then one night, she had a dream. A radiant Kibo appeared before her, golden ears of wheat shimmering behind it. The Kibo spoke to her: "True abundance is not brought forth by the magic of a tool, but lies within respect and care for the earth. Feel the heartbeat of the land with your own heart—only then can you truly live in harmony with it."
Upon waking, Eileen reflected on her actions and urged the villagers to let the land rest. Pooling their wisdom together, the villagers learned about crop rotation and fallowing, strictly observing the designated periods of rest for the soil. After several moons of patient effort, the fields finally regained their vitality and yielded a long-awaited, bountiful harvest.

Material: Sturdy overall with a stable structure. Its moderate hardness makes it easy to mine and cut. Even after processing, it remains intact for long periods and does not rapidly deteriorate from moisture or weathering.
Formation: Often forms among cool, damp rock strata. The ore contains microscopic crystals capable of storing faint light, which gradually develop into a stable, uniform luminescent structure through prolonged deposition and compaction.
Uses: A relatively common stone that can be worked into quality building blocks. Frequently used in the construction of houses, walls, and roads.

1518783: Author's Note: "Cheshirebat's Bedtime Fables" is a collection of stories that surfaced roughly four hundred cycles ago, said to have been burned as a banned book during a certain era. Consequently, only scattered fragments have survived to the present day. The tales within represent an over-interpretation of actual Kibo behavior. Unlike sapient races, Kibo should not be subjected to excessive subjective speculation or imagination in scholarly research. Nevertheless, I believe such works hold intrinsic value and deserve to be collected as a literary genre in their own right. Thus, I traveled across the continent to compile and republish them in a single volume. In truth, I do not recommend reading these to children as bedtime stories, yet curious Kibo researchers and lovers of tales may uncover new hypotheses and possibilities within these pages. I Became a Greytarg— "Stuffed with wheat, stuffed with wheat, my belly's round and causes a fuss. Here comes a Schnelf to swallow me up, nowhere to run, nowhere to hide." He was the fattest, most bloated Greytarg in the world. His belly swelled like a balloon as he holed up in one spot, utterly motionless, unable even to roll over. He had a dreadful temper. If a single grain of wheat had so much as a speck of dust on it, he would snort furiously, blowing white puffs from his nose and scattering all the wheat the Grainards had just offered him. The poor Grainards would then have to set out again to gather spotless grains, running back and forth so often that their claws wore down. Even then, the Greytarg wasn't satisfied; with his eyes squeezed shut, he would order the trembling Grainies to crawl beneath his rear, and then crush them flat with all his might. Fearing his strength and authority, the Grainies and Grainards served this fattest, most bloated Greytarg without rest. As a result, they all grew gaunt, as thin as parched stalks of straw. I couldn't understand why everyone accepted such a life. I looked at the grains in my paws. This was food I had worked so hard to gather—why wasn't I allowed to eat it myself instead of offering it up to that bloated nuisance? Unable to hold back, I asked the Grainies and Grainards beside me: "Why do we hand all our food over to him?" The Grainies and Grainards exchanged glances. "That's just how we've always lived." "We're so weak, we can't survive without relying on the Greytarg. He protects us." "In return, it's only right that we offer him our food." They all chirped in unison. "But he's never protected us even once! All he does is steal our wheat—" Before I could finish speaking, a terrifying howl echoed from afar—a Schnelf! One, two... Schnelf cries rang out from every direction. We were surrounded! I led everyone racing back toward the Greytarg's territory, hoping we could shake off these dangerous predators. Yet the Schnelfs gave relentless chase, showing no intention of letting us escape. More and more Grainies and Grainards joined our fleeing band, while only the Greytarg stayed behind. Was he planning to hold the rear? Along with a blood-curdling shriek from the Greytarg, the Schnelfs stopped pursuing us. Layer upon layer of tall grass hid the Greytarg's bloated form as he shrank smaller and smaller in our sight. It was plain to everyone that he wouldn't survive. "See? The Greytarg protected us," one of the Grainards told me. The Grainies and Grainards looked terribly sad. One Grainy said, "I shed a tear for the Greytarg." Another Grainy said, "Well, I shed three whole tears!" Together, they gathered around me. "With the Greytarg gone, what are we supposed to do? You're the Grainard who led us to safety from the Schnelf attack... Please, become our great king!" But I shook my head. "I don't want to become a Greytarg. I don't want to end up that fat and lazy. Besides, I think we should share all the wheat we gather equally." They didn't reject my idea, and together we built a new home in another wheat field. They listened closely to everything I said. If I mentioned there ought to be a swing woven from wheat leaves to the east, a swing would appear in the east; if I said there should be a granary to the west, a spacious granary would be built in the west. Sometimes they would even slip me grains of wheat on the sly. At first, it was just one Grainy secretly giving me half his share; I figured it was a gesture of goodwill and half wouldn't hurt. Soon after, though, even the Grainards began offering me food, and I couldn't bring myself to refuse, so I had no choice but to eat the grains. I am a Grainard, after all—I simply can't resist the taste of wheat. Little by little, I grew lazy and plump. My tail lengthened and dragged behind me, until at last I became the fattest, most bloated Greytarg of all. I grew short-tempered, and my head felt stuffed to the brim with nothing but wheat. I snorted white puffs from my nose and roared with my eyes: "Bring me wheat, bring me wheat! If you don't bring me wheat, I'll sit on every last one of you and squash you flat!" Like my servants, they bowed in reverence and dutifully offered me every single grain they harvested. And then, once again, the cries of Schnelfs echoed out. One, two... They tightened their encirclement around my territory. I wanted to flee at once, yet my body was far too heavy, my head too weighty to lift, and my limbs felt rooted to the earth. The Grainies and Grainards bolted past me at breakneck speed, leaving me the only one unable to move. Only a single Grainy looked back at me once as he fled. He said to me— "Dear Greytarg, I shed a tear for you." (*At the very end, a single line of commentary is written: Perhaps what truly rules over them is the golden ears of wheat.)

[Preface]
Bluevine (also known as Reddeem) is a distinctive cash crop native to the Branzea region of the Rosia Empire. Roughly one hundred cycles ago, orchardists in Fleece attempted to introduce and cultivate it, gradually breeding varieties suited to Fleece's climate. Today, it has become one of Fleece's signature local specialties.
Bluevine possesses a trait extraordinarily rare among plants: it bears fruit once every two cycles, yet its harvest season depends on when it is planted. If planted in winter, it is harvested in winter, yielding fruit of a deep azure hue. If planted in summer, it is harvested the following cycle's summer, yielding fruit of a vibrant vermilion—which is why Bluevine is also called "Reddeem."
Large and plump, Bluevine berries offer a sweet, refreshing flavor and a crisp aroma, making them delightfully easy to eat. Furthermore, processed Bluevine serves well as an ingredient in confections and cuisine, and when brewed into beverages, it develops a unique sweet-and-tart profile. For this reason, it has earned the nickname "Edible Gem" and enjoys an endless stream of admirers—including even certain Kibo who are fond of its taste.
Despite Bluevine's high economic value, its unusual two-cycle cultivation and demanding environmental needs intimidate many orchardists, who shy away before even trying. This volume, "A Guide to Viticulture," aims to present practical Bluevine cultivation techniques in clear, concise language across ten chapters covering cultivar selection, sapling propagation, vineyard layout, water and fertilizer management, pruning and training, and blossom and fruit care. Richly illustrated throughout, it is designed to be accessible and practical.

1518790: Preface It goes without saying that we intelligent beings could never have unraveled all the mysteries of the world in a mere few thousand moons of history. The continent of Promilia is brimming with wonders far beyond our imagination, with countless secrets slumbering from sky to sea. Recording these secrets and sharing them with the world is the very duty entrusted to the Unsolved Mysteries Editorial Department. We hope that one day, these secrets will no longer remain "Unsolved Mysteries." Most people have yet to recognize the significance of such records, and at times, parties with vested interests have even interfered with our investigations. Printing and publishing the Unsolved Mysteries series met with many hardships, yet through our department's relentless efforts, we have finally compiled the series into book form. Volumes in this series are hidden near various "Unsolved Mysteries" across the land, waiting to fall into the hands of those who seek the truth. We believe that anyone who finds this book shares our aspirations and carries a burning passion for discovery. Dear readers, please remember that on your journey in pursuit of the truth, the Unsolved Mysteries Editorial Department is always walking beside you. Volume 1: Pammy's Trapdoor ... Every Pammy's Miracle Workshop has always had a tiny trapdoor. It is just the right size for a Pammy to slip through—anyone even slightly larger would get stuck and unable to move. Whether in the Pammy's Miracle Workshop in Fleece, the one in the Chen Dynasty, or the one in Reve—in every Pammy's Miracle Workshop across the world, this trapdoor exists, yet no one has ever seen it open. The trapdoor in Pammy's Miracle Workshop is always shut tight. I once asked the Pammy working at the reception desk of Pammy's Miracle Workshop what this trapdoor was for. The Pammy answered with their signature smile: "Beneath the trapdoor lies a Pammy secret! Hmm, you want to know what secret it is? Well... of course I can't tell you~" That Pammy's smile was so adorable that I instantly forgot the question weighing on my mind. Everyone, I love Pammies! Even when a Pammy isn't doing anything and just hops along past me, I find them unbearably cute. Just seeing a Pammy smile makes me feel as though I've been born anew. And that tiny secret hidden beneath the trapdoor only makes Pammies seem even more mysterious and endearing. Wait... why do I like Pammies this much? Come to think of it, no one seems to know where Pammies come from or where they go. We simply accept their existence, just as Promilia has accepted us all. I understand that every race has its own secrets. Perhaps the secret of the Pammies simply takes the shape of a trapdoor. Thinking about Pammy's trapdoor, I fell into a deep slumber. In my dream, the trapdoor swung open, and countless Pammies poured out, swallowing me whole. Since that night, Pammies have been all I can think about. If I go a whole day without seeing a Pammy, my entire body grows sluggish and I cannot sleep. After that, I began sneaking into Pammy's Miracle Workshop every day, secretly watching the Pammies and that trapdoor. I feel like there is something else I ought to be doing. I feel like I'm supposed to be investigating the secrets of this world. I feel like I'm supposed to be writing a book together with my colleagues. Yet such thoughts cross my mind less and less. Lately, looking at my reflection in the mirror makes me feel slightly uneasy. Why am I an ordinary human, and not a Pammy? Don't misunderstand—I don't hate myself, nor do I hold any prejudice against other races. It's just that I have to be a Pammy. I want to be one of the Pammies. I want to be part of the Pammy family. I want to enter Pammy's Miracle Workshop. I want to become a Pammy. I want to become nothing but a Pammy. Tonight, I am heading to Pammy's Miracle Workshop. There, I will... This is the final letter left behind by Investigator Rasha of the Unsolved Mysteries Editorial Department before her disappearance. Afterward, all contact from her ceased. In light of this, out of concern for our staff's safety, we have suspended all investigations into Pammy's trapdoors. Whatever the outcome may be, we sincerely hope Investigator Rasha has found the happiness she wished for.

1518796:
My grandfather, Moriles Monquet, was one of the most renowned shipwrights in Gondoro—more than half the boats still afloat in town owed their construction to his hands. Influenced by him, I was captivated by boats from a young age. Back then, my happiest moments were spent sitting in the cabin watching Grandfather pull at the oars. He told me countless legends about ships, rivers, and the sea, though sadly Fleece lies far inland. Thus, I could never lay eyes upon the ocean myself and had to fill in the rest of his tales with my imagination. All of Grandfather's stories began the same way: "Long, long ago—I couldn't say how many moons ago, only that it was in the distant past..."
"Long, long ago—I couldn't say how many moons ago, only that it was in the distant past... perhaps even before the era when the Dragonkin ruled... the world did not yet look as it does today, and every creature upon the land lived a harsh life. In those days, the skies were forever shrouded in gloomy mist, and even flying Kibos feared soaring too high, for no one knew what lurked above those gray clouds. Yet intelligent beings were never content to stay rooted in place... though that's just a pretty way of putting it—in truth, humanity kept growing and simply had no choice but to pioneer new settlements. Little Eric, you know as well as anyone that water is essential for survival! That's why people always built new villages near water sources... And so rivers, seas, and springs wove our destinies together, right down to this very day—and that is why I love boats."
Alas, my dear Grandfather, the passage of time has far outpaced anything we could have imagined. Time altered the course of rivers, cleared the skies, and gave birth to airships and countless new technologies. Like a drifting vessel, the town of Gondoro was swept along by the current of the ages, gradually fading into the river of history.
My two closest friends, Nankaro and Bettirica, left Gondoro with their parents long ago. Even the boats that once served as their homes were hauled away and sold off. Nankaro is now immersed in studying the state religion of the Rosia Empire and its holy light magic, while Bettirica departed for Itone and never sent a single letter back... Grandfather, do you still believe that the sea and the waters bind people's fates together?
I know you can no longer answer any of my questions... At your funeral three days ago, I watched the coffin lid close with my own eyes and laid a bouquet upon your gravestone. In your youth, you contributed so much to this town. Because of that, many people returned to Gondoro on the day of your funeral to bid you farewell—even those who had left long ago. Uncle Roberto came back too. He looked leaner and more sun-darkened than before, yet seemed far livelier than he ever had in town. He told me all about his life after leaving Gondoro—how he traveled to Qiyun and rode the Island-Ring Train that dives beneath the sea, and how he found work as a guide in the Rosinia Federation, spending every day aboard airships...
By now, I have navigated every last waterway winding through Gondoro. Just like you, I know every inch of a boat's frame, and I have dreamed countless dreams amid the swaying waves. Only tonight, I can no longer dream of those old legends—perhaps my time to leave has finally come as well.
Unlike Nankaro, Bettirica, and Uncle Roberto, I do not want to vanish from Gondoro as though I had never existed at all. That is why I have decided to leave behind this small boat we built together, along with a farewell letter never meant to reach anyone.
May we meet again someday in the sea where all rivers converge.

1518800: Fleece Street NewsNo. 034Special Report: A Day at the Lord's ManorEarly morning in Fleece was wrapped in a pleasant hush. From the moment my editor told me last night, "I want you to shadow Nanacha at the Lord's Manor," my heart soared as high as a Mokyun, and my steps grew noticeably lighter. Today, as I knocked on the manor doors, the reality of it finally sank in. Nanacha and the manor's butler, Mr. Shine, already had warm tea waiting. "You are our first guest today. The visitors from Eldenland are scheduled to arrive in an hour. Please help yourself to the tea and refreshments in the parlor until then." True to her reputation as Head Maid, Nanacha's attentiveness and meticulous work ethic are sure to win praise from every single visitor. It is said that Nanacha has worked at the manor since before the current Lord took office. When it comes to knowledge of the manor, if she claimed to be second best, no one would dare claim to be first. Following her around today proved that beyond a shadow of a doubt. At 9:50 a.m., ten minutes before the next guests arrived, Nanacha led the maids in straightening the carpets once more and setting out fresh refreshments. The freshly brewed specialty fragrant tea was at the ideal drinking temperature, the table was polished to a mirror sheen, and the organized business documents were neatly arranged before the Lord's seat. Nanacha even kept an eye on the shifting light outside the windows, adjusting the curtains accordingly. "Count Bourgeois is deeply concerned—anxious, even—about next quarter's ore procurement and the related trade partnership. I hope the aroma of the fragrant tea and the gentle lighting will put him at ease, even just a little," Nanacha explained. Once the Lord and Count Bourgeois began their negotiations, Head Maid Nanacha waited in the anteroom, keeping alert in case anything was needed in the parlor while helping Mr. Shine sort through letters received from citizens over the past week. Among them were complaints regarding public safety and municipal affairs, as well as gifts from residents. Nanacha explained: "The Lord's sheriffs and guards do everything in their power to protect citizens' livelihoods. However, whenever people have suggestions for city management or run into problems that are hard to resolve, they can also write directly to the Lord for advice. The Lord reads every single letter. Serving the citizens is our duty, after all." In the afternoon, Nanacha helped process event applications submitted by various organizers before beginning a thorough cleaning of the entire manor. Tablecloths and cushions were sent to the laundry room, the floors were swept and dry-mopped to a spotless finish, and the water in every vase was replaced. No matter how trivial the task, Nanacha never lost her gentle smile. "Keeping the manor clean and ensuring everyone feels comfortable is my greatest joy." Night fell, and the workday drew to a close. With all of today's duties at the manor complete, my report was nearing its end as well. Before seeing me out, Nanacha handed me a gift she had prepared in advance. Gentleness, professionalism, generosity, and sincerity—throughout our time together, I felt a rare and profound charm in Nanacha that few possess. No wonder she's the Pammy who took first place in the "Fleece Ambassador Candidates" popularity poll!
1518801:
At first, the snowflakes were no larger than fingernails, but soon they whirled like feathers, piling into ever thicker drifts. It was the dead of winter. Across the desolate frontier snowfields where no one ever set foot, not a single patch of bare ground remained uncovered by ice, and scarcely any living thing could survive this white world of death. The Kibos had either entered hibernation or migrated to warmer lands. All that remained by Sergey's side was a herd of Gayaks. The Gayaks were his sole companions here, silently and steadfastly enduring every hardship fate thrust upon them.
The Gayaks never complained. In spring, they grazed on the tender moss growing upon the frozen soil; in autumn, they ate the hay Sergey had stored away. And now that winter had arrived, they neither ate nor drank, merely pressing quietly against Sergey's side with gleaming, watery eyes. The only warm "white" drifting through the air was the "white mist" of breath exhaled by Gadoli and the Gayaks freezing in the bitter wind.
Yet from time to time, even the Gayaks shed tears.
Sergey gazed coldly at the blizzard raging outside. Though it was still daytime, he could barely see ten paces ahead. It was as if everything in the world had vanished save the crude wooden cabin he stood in—including the sins he bore and the salvation forever beyond his reach. On clear days, he would stare intently at the low, rolling mountains stretching across the edge of the snowfield, as though his gaze could fly past this land of suffering all the way to the bustling, warm capital. He wondered why he had to suffer here while others danced joyful waltzes at grand balls. Yet whenever he remembered his sins, Sergey's spirit faltered. He could not shake the feeling that the dead lay buried beneath the snow—that the moment he stepped outside, pale-blue hands of the dead would reach out and drag him down into an endless hell.
Still, there was nothing to fear, Sergey thought. This place was already hell.
Just then, something brushed gently against his palm. Looking down, Sergey saw it was a Gayak's muzzle.
The Gayak gazed up at him, and a single tear fell from its dark eyes. Gayaks possessed well-developed tear glands to keep their eyes from drying out too much. Yes, Kibos didn't cry out of sorrow; it was merely a conditioned reflex. That was what Sergey told himself. Yet in a corner of his heart, he felt as though a saint were looking at him through the Gayak's eyes, weeping for his sins.
O Holy One, if you truly exist...
Sergey prayed silently within his heart. Please, grant me...
1518803:
"Let's pick this one!"
Standing in the sunlight, Amy raised her right hand high. Clutched in her palm was a golden ear of wheat, plump and heavy with grain. Margaret gave a slight nod and took the wheat from Amy.
Amy stared at her older sister's back. Days of hard labor had left her shoulders slightly hunched. Her curly blonde hair was hastily tied back and tucked into her hood, and the dress she wore was covered in patches. A pang of sorrow swelled in Amy's chest, and she called out before she could stop herself:
"Margaret—let me help!"
Margaret had already hung the golden wheat over the front door. With the Golden Wheat Carnival approaching, every household was busy preparing. This bundle Amy had chosen was lovelier than any before it, giving Margaret a quiet premonition that this cycle would bring a bountiful harvest.
Keeping her back to Amy, she pointed toward the house.
"Go check on Lucy. She wasn't feeling well this morning and barely ate a thing."
Amy turned and stepped inside the cottage.
The wooden floorboards gave a familiar creak beneath her feet. Amy had lived here her whole life; her family had lived in this home for generations. The cottage had been patched and repaired so many times that the timber holding it together was likely completely different from what it had been a hundred cycles ago. Yet the Wimbledons were still here. On the cupboard shelves stood row after row of small ceramic figurines sculpted by Caroline—a farmer stooping to till the soil, a Bangoose foraging in a wheat field, and countless other pieces. Under Caroline's skillful hands, every one of them seemed alive and breathing.
Amy smiled as she looked over the figurines. She had always believed in her younger sister's talent. If only Caroline had one chance to exhibit her work—just once—she would surely make a name for herself in Fleece. The only problem was figuring out where to find such an opportunity.
"Big sis..."
It was Lucy's voice. Amy quickly pushed her thoughts aside and headed to the bedroom. Lucy was the youngest of the Wimbledon sisters, quiet and introverted. She loved sitting by the window with a pen in hand, writing down whatever came to mind. Yet she was neither lively nor strong, often falling ill with fevers and coughs. Amy hadn't heard her coughing today, but she decided to bring her a cup of warm tea anyway.
"What's wrong, Lucy?"
Lucy turned her large, thoughtful blue eyes toward her. Usually dreamy and distant, they held a touch of earnestness now.
"I don't want to go to school anymore. My hair hurts really bad."
She said it in all seriousness.
Amy blinked in puzzlement.
Her hair? Perhaps this was just a new excuse Lucy had invented to skip school—or perhaps Lucy had something else on her mind entirely. 

(Small penciled notes written along the bottom of the manuscript paper) The four Wimbledon sisters: Margaret, the calm and somewhat strict eldest; Amy, lively and quick-witted; Caroline, the passionate artist; and Lucy, the shy and withdrawn youngest who harbors literary dreams and constantly worries about the family's finances...
Hmm, this story just popped into my head one day. Maybe I should write it down... Maybe someone might even publish it... No, my writing is still far too rough—nobody would ever want to read it... Still, I want to try writing it...
1518805: Yesterday's Tears and Tomorrow's ThornsA Serious Drama in Four Acts CharactersNikolai Andreyevich — A retired teacher. Igor Nikolayevich — His son, deceased. Elena Viktorovna — His daughter-in-law, deceased. Sofia Igorevna — His granddaughter, a former conservatory student who dropped out. Act IA living room. An old wooden desk and two chairs stand inside; a candle casts a dim glow, and faint flames flicker in the hearth. On the desk sit a teacup, several sheets of paper, a quill, and an uncapped inkwell. In the corner, a Snobow lies curled up asleep. Wearing spectacles, Nikolai sits at the desk leafing through a bundle of letters. Sofia paces back and forth across the room. Sofia Grandfather! Stop staring at those old letters! Since that day... has anyone sent us a single letter since that day? Nikolai Past memories do not fade with the passing of time. Sofia (Laughs coldly) Open your eyes! If you cared at all, you would notice the fire in the hearth is dying. Surely you can tell we are about to freeze to death! Your precious old memories are good for nothing except burning in the fire to keep us warm! Nikolai Wait just a little longer. I want to commit these letters to memory... Sofia Your students forgot about you long ago. Nikolai I remember every single one of them. Sofia Then do you remember that your students were the ones who signed that decree? Your son—my father—was killed in that upheaval. And yet you still fancy yourself the respected old professor admired by his pupils? They murdered our family, treated us like ashes from burnt firewood, and cast us into a forgotten corner of the world. If I could, I would lose myself in dreams of the past just like you. But someone has to keep their eyes open just to keep this little cabin from falling apart! Do you know how those people look at us? With pity mixed with contempt. They put on a show of saying how pitiful we are, while deep down they think we got what we deserved. Oh, if only I could vanish like April snow... where no one would ever see me... [Sofia stops and buries her face in her hands, weeping.] Nikolai Sofia... my dear child, go ahead and cry all you need. Sofia Why don't you ever cry? I have never once seen your tears... Nikolai My tears dried up long ago. Come, take these—let the past give us warmth one last time. [Sofia takes the bundle of letters from Nikolai's hands and tosses them into the hearth. The flames flare brightly for a moment, then slowly die down again.] Sofia And my sheet music... it's thick enough to burn all night... Nikolai Keep your sheet music. Sofia It's fine, I've already memorized all of it. Nikolai Hold on to it. We will get through this. [The Snobow in the corner wakes up and pads over to Sofia.] Nikolai Sing for me, dear. Your voice has always made us forget our troubles. Sofia I haven't practiced singing in days. Nikolai Even so, your voice is as lovely as ever. [Sofia scoops the Snobow into her arms and begins humming softly. The Snobow drifts off to sleep.]
1518806:
This happened long, long ago—yet not at the dawn of wisdom itself. People tirelessly sought new knowledge, though it was, in truth, a perilous pursuit. Seeking secrets meant reaching blindly into the dark and groping for the unknown. Once all easily reachable wisdom had been exhausted, some chose to remain within the safe haven of what was already understood, content to merely observe the edges of the dark mysteries—after all, the technologies they had already developed afforded them an amply prosperous life.
Yet there were also scholars and wandering travelers. Firmly believing that the pursuit of knowledge was the very purpose of life, they crossed mountains and forded rivers in endless search of an untouched sanctuary where they could cultivate wisdom to its depths. At last, they halted in a land lush with greenery yet somehow desolate, and set about building a new home. Little did they know, however, that a race bearing an ancient bloodline slumbered within this land. The sounds of new life stirring caught the attention of the young Rafau. Noticing the travelers bustling at their work, they hid among the marshes, beneath the shade of trees, and within the reedbeds, watching a new city take shape... and then, fluttering their fledgling wings, they returned to the leader of the ancient bloodline to report again and again on the travelers' tireless devotion.
"Watch closely to see whether, once they taste setback, they can face the greater trials prepared by living creatures and nature with courage and patience."
Not long after the divine beast spoke this prophecy, the city was struck by a tempest of lightning. Amid bolts streaking across the sky and thunder piercing the clouds, the tall towers the travelers had raised groaned, and their stained-glass windows shattered. Everything splendid and beautiful was wiped away, and their new home was reduced to scorched earth.
"An excessive thirst for knowledge is no different from excessive greed. Perhaps this is our punishment," said one traveler.
"Yet to cast aside knowledge is to cast aside one's soul," another traveler replied.
"Do you not fear greed?"
"I desire knowledge more."
The Rafau and the leader of the ancient bloodline overheard their exchange. Though the travelers sank briefly into sorrow, they soon resumed their studies, throwing themselves back into rebuilding, designing, and constructing... until sturdier homes rose once more. The travelers never naively assumed that peaceful days would simply continue from then on. Knowledge itself was their weapon. At last, in this land called Avarian, lightning once again passed merciless judgment upon the travelers.
"I want to go help them," said a Rafau, beginning to spread its still-soft wings.
"Do you not fear the lightning?" The leader's voice boomed louder than the thunder.
"I desire the lightning!" The Rafau soared high into the sky. The electric charge clinging to its body disrupted the path of the storm clouds, drawing the lightning bolts in pursuit of its shadow. For the first time, it tasted this power—a power meant to be one with its very being. Its body lengthened and grew slender, horns and a tail began to sprout, and its claws sharpened... As it danced amidst the lightning, the skies cleared once more, and the travelers gazed in awe and respect at this majestic Radiva.
"Thank you for protecting this land."
"I merely share the same thirst as you."
The Radiva walked up to the travelers who had stayed true to their pursuit of knowledge. The young Rafau nestled beside their leader raised their heads. "It chose its own companions, didn't it?"
"It chose radiant souls," the leader answered.
1518807:
Blue flames. They were flames burning with eerie ferocity in the dark of night. Genjiro stopped in his tracks. Even as he felt a dread unlike any he had ever known, a powerful curiosity welled up within him.
Long before he lost his way in this forest, he had been lost for ages. His glorious past and his fallen clan bound him night after night like a lingering dream.
"What meaning can there possibly be in a life like this?"
As he pondered this, he heard a faint cry. At times low, at times high, the voice seemed to speak of untold secrets. Drawn by that mysterious sound, he followed it until he laid eyes upon blue flames unlike anything he had ever seen.
A colossal black shadow lurked in the treetops, blue flames blazing fiercely above its head. Genjiro stared at the towering silhouette, trying to find an answer within its cries.
Perhaps sensing Genjiro's gaze, the shadow ceased its crying and turned around, fixing Genjiro with its ethereal eyes.
In that instant, he felt an indescribable sense of connection—as though some fateful bond existed between this great black shadow and himself.
The dark silhouette let out another cry, one that seemed to carry a message. Holding his breath, Genjiro focused intently, trying to decipher the mystical voice.
"Is that voice... trying to tell me something?" he asked softly.
As if understanding Genjiro's words, the voice grew clearer—"I am Driftshadow, emissary of the night."
"Canst thou hear my voice?"
Gazing up at Driftshadow, Genjiro replied, "I hear it... the breath of the forest, the whispers of the night."
At that moment, Driftshadow's blue flames blazed higher, as if praising Genjiro's answer.
"Is thy blade still honed as sharply as in days of old?" Driftshadow suddenly asked.
Genjiro gripped the hilt of his katana and answered, "Ever constant as the moon, deep as the night."
Driftshadow let out a long cry, spread its wings, and took flight. A howling wind swept through the desolate forest, and the blue flames vanished into the woods' depths. And vanishing along with them was the figure of the warrior who had once been mired in despair.
1518808:
On the busiest street in town, a newly opened toy shop was drawing everyone's attention. Inside, plushies of all kinds—from giant bears to tiny rabbits—were lined up in neat rows, every single one of them adorable. Hearing the rumors, Mofurine's curiosity was piqued once again.
Letting out a cheerful "Nini~," it decided to peek inside the toy shop.

"Mommy, look! This plushie is so cute!"
"Daddy! It feels so nice to hug—I want this one!"
Flying secretly into the shop, Mofurine watched all the children happily hugging the plushies, and a sudden idea struck it—
"Maybe I should turn into a plushie too and let everyone hug me! That's gotta feel amazing!"
So, using its mysterious power, Mofurine transformed into a tiny figure indistinguishable from a stuffed toy and blended right in among the plushies.
Before long, several more children wandered into the toy shop one after another. Everyone cheered and happily held up the cute plushies, eager to give them all a squeeze.
When one child wrapped Mofurine in a tight hug in its plushie form, it felt a warmth and comfort unlike anything it had ever known. The sensation was so blissful that it couldn't help but start purring!
"Huh? Why is this plushie purring?" the child asked in surprise.
The other children and adults in the shop gathered around, staring in wonder at the purring plushie. Realizing its cover was blown, Mofurine shyly reverted to its true form. Its eight ears swayed gently, and a mischievous sparkle glinted in its eyes.
"Nini~" Mofurine greeted everyone with its signature cry and did a joyful somersault in midair.
"Whoa! A flying plushie!"
"No, no, isn't that a Kibo?"
"I've seen it in a book! That's a Mofurine! It's definitely a Mofurine!"
The children erupted into cheers. Never in their wildest dreams had they expected to actually meet the legendary Mofurine! From that day on, Mofurine was no longer a secret—it became the most popular star in town.
And thanks to Mofurine's tale, the toy shop became the children's favorite spot as well. Everyone knows that not only can you find adorable plushies there, you might even run into the real Mofurine. And Mofurine still returns to the toy shop from time to time, transforming into a plushie to enjoy the warmth of being hugged.
Of course, by now it has learned how to control its purring, so it doesn't give itself away quite so easily anymore.
1518810:
At the borders of a faraway sacred lake lies a sanctuary blessed with eternal morning light and watery mist. It is the domain of Shiropoko—a place radiating holy brilliance while harboring an overwhelming power.
Shiropoko is a Kibo with two horns atop its head and four large ears swaying in the morning breeze. When dawn breaks and the first golden rays shimmer across the water's surface, it always emerges quietly from the hazy mist.
"Within this sanctuary, Shiropoko is the one and only sovereign," an elder from a nearby village would always tell the restless youths.

The elder had once heard a tale like this—

One morning, a painter visited the lakeshore. Hoping to capture the wondrous sight of the lake at dawn, he set up his easel and eagerly began painting the interplay of rippling water and morning glow.
He did not notice that on a rock a short distance away, a soft silhouette had quietly perched itself and was watching him with keen curiosity.
Blinking, Shiropoko gently lifted its head and tried mimicking the painter's gestures. It puffed out its chest, stretched its neck, narrowed its eyes to gaze into the distance, and even imitated the pose of holding a brush with its forepaw.
That "majestic" posture made it feel even closer to a "lofty light"—or so Shiropoko believed.
Just then, a mischievous little beast sprang out from the lakeside reeds, letting out a shrill cry!
Startled, the painter spun around—and saw it. An "avatar of sacred light" that ought to belong high in the heavens was crouching right nearby, imitating him with a look of pride on its face.
In his fluster, the brush slipped from his hand, sending a splash of lake water onto Shiropoko's fur.
"Poko," a low, trembling sound rippled across the water. Shiropoko's eyes flashed sharply.
As the star patterns across its body erupted in a dazzling golden-white glow, every strand of its fur stood on end, transforming into slender, razor-sharp spears of light. The lake's surface rippled under the surge of energy, and the morning mist tore apart to reveal a breathtaking golden vista.
The painter trembled before the sudden divine radiance. Unable to rise, he could only shield his eyes with both hands. Meanwhile, the little beast bolted in panic back into the tall grass.
"Poko!" Shiropoko's voice echoed between wind and water. Like both a whisper and the tolling of a bell, it carried an irresistible majesty, as though warning mortals not to trespass into its sanctuary.
Leaping upward, Shiropoko became a pale-blue afterimage, streaking straight toward the heavens as trails of stardust-like light rained down upon the lake.
Mist slowly drifted back over the water, and the radiance gradually faded, as if the entire encounter had been nothing more than a mirage of dawn.
The painter stared blankly at the lake. All he could see were his ruined canvas and the faint ripples still swaying on the water's surface.
His memories were gone. He could not recall a single trace of Shiropoko's form.

"Remember this well, children,"
the elder said beside the crackling campfire. "If ever you hear a soft, soul-stirring 'Poko' amidst the morning mist and lake light, it is neither the breeze nor a waterfowl. It is the sovereign of the sanctuary proclaiming its domain."

1518813:
You often hear people say that the crop circles of Fleece are nothing more than hoaxes made to draw in tourists. Surely some of them are—the Fleece residents caught in the act of making them are proof enough of that. Yet I want to state loud and clear that we must not let a few examples mislead us. From my own personal experience at least—mark me, my own personal experience—I can guarantee that some are truly not made by human hands. What I am about to tell you is why.
I was taking my usual stroll through the wheat fields when, all of a sudden, I felt an inexplicable pressure. At first I dismissed it as my imagination and paid it no mind. Soon, however, I realized something was terribly wrong. The pressure intensified rapidly, and within moments, the wheat around me slowly began to flatten. Stranger still, once the wheat before me had been pressed down to a certain extent, the pressure did not seem to reach even a few meters farther ahead—the stalks there showed no sign of bending at all. I tried to make sense of what was happening, yet by then the pressure had turned painful. I even felt as though it were beginning to seep inside my body!
The pressure spread slowly from my head down to my toes. Breathing grew difficult, and my thoughts dulled. My legs began to move clumsily, though whether out of instinct or something else entirely, I cannot say. I had no memory of commanding myself to move. I could no longer even tell what I was thinking. My mouth must have hung open, for I felt air drifting across my tongue. Air fought desperately to enter my body, yet only the thinnest trickle could get through. Was I even the one breathing? What was that clattering sound? What was resting upon my shoulders?
The pressure soaked into every corner of my body. My very soul was going to be forced out!
Suddenly, I collapsed to the ground, gasping violently for air. A breeze carrying the scent of wheat and dust swept straight through me in an instant. A gentle wind filled my body, and everything felt weightless. Though thinking was still difficult, I knew the pressure had left me. I tried to get up to see what had saved me, yet my limbs refused to obey, leaving me lying flat on my stomach.
After a while, I managed to prop myself up on my arms. It still hurt, yet at least I could shift from lying face-down to sitting upright, making it easier to look around. The moment I glanced back the way I had come, however, I was left speechless. A broad expanse of wheat lay flattened. The sight reminded me of the crop circles I had seen before—yet it was not quite the same. The wheat before me had been pressed down far more forcefully than any circle I had ever witnessed, lying almost glued to the earth. I may have been present at the exact moment a real crop circle was formed! Realizing this, I scanned my surroundings for any clue. Yet aside from a tiny light visible at the far edge of the sky, I found nothing at all.
Of course, if after reading this tale you still refuse to believe in crop circles not made by human hands, I respect your view. My experience was undeniably bizarre. Just remember this one piece of advice—if you ever find yourself in the same predicament, move at once toward the undisturbed wheat.

1518823:
...How did Fleece Valley regain its vitality so rapidly after the war? Beyond the indomitable spirit of the ancient pioneers, there is one existence that cannot possibly be overlooked—the Kibo known as "Amalthea."
According to surviving fragments of the "Pioneer Chronicles," two thousand cycles ago, when the city walls of Fleece were first raised and reclamation began, Amalthea was already active in the valley. At the time, Fleece's soil was barren and its water sources were murky. No matter how tirelessly the pioneers labored day and night, their harvests remained poor. It was Amalthea's intervention during those trying times that brought a turning point to this land.
Rather than simply "granting" something, what Amalthea did was closer to "restoration"—using power derived from Water Starvein energy, it purified rivers tainted by war, returned nutrients to the soil, and transformed wasteland unfit for farming into fertile earth. One record claims that wherever Amalthea's tears fell, fresh shoots sprouted even from barren gravel. The endless waves of wheat that Fleece prides itself on today stand upon this very foundation.
However, Amalthea never seemed to seek a closer bond with humans. As the city-state of Fleece grew ever more prosperous and reclamation efforts stabilized, Amalthea gradually faded from public view. According to accounts from the early pioneers, the last place Amalthea was sighted was around Meltlake, and for hundreds of cycles since, scarcely anyone has laid eyes on its true form.
Judging from surviving texts, Amalthea's demonstrated abilities center primarily on two things: purifying water sources and accelerating plant growth. Its power was gentle and enduring, with not a single record of it ever harming people or livestock. Without question, it was a true guardian.
1518824:
Children, have you ever wondered why Fleece's wheat shines a richer gold than any other, and why its river water is clearer and sweeter?
It is because long, long ago, several gentle guardians lived right here.
And one of them was Amalthea. Its body was said to be longer than ten Krodimes lined up end to end, with a crystalline crown of horns upon its head, drifting softly through the air cloaked in a watery shimmer like stardust.
Amalthea is a Kibo that brought blessings to this land.
Back then, Fleece had just endured a great war. The earth was scorched black—not even wild grass grew, let alone crops. Though tormented by hunger, those who worked to clear the land sowed seeds and watered them. Yet no one knew if they would harvest enough food by autumn to survive the winter.
Then one night, Amalthea appeared. No one saw where it came from. Only in the moonlight did someone catch a glimpse of its glowing form in the distance. It gazed upon the cracked earth, gazed upon the dried-up riverbed, and shed a single tear.
Where that tear fell, the very first flower in postwar Fleece bloomed.
From then on, the river waters began to clear, the soil grew fertile, and the seeds they had planted sprouted strong and true. Yet Amalthea did not depart; it lingered on distant hills and lakeshores, watching over them as they tilled the fields and built Fleece up piece by piece.
Today, Fleece flourishes more than ever, with mills standing tall and granaries filled. Even so, we must never forget that it was Amalthea who once brought pure springs to Fleece and breathed life back into this land...

Dear Ma. It's already been half a cycle since I left home and arrived at Juxia Pass. I hope you're doing well back home. That half-cycle flew by in a flash. During this time, my comrades and I have been training hard, and I'm starting to see some real progress. Forget marching and fighting—even when I come home to work the fields, I've got way more strength in me than before!

About the war you asked about in your last letter—that's military confidential, so I can't tell you. Still, the Chief Instructor told us our purpose in training here is to one day fight the Fiendbeasts bravely and protect our country and families. If the Fiendbeasts really do attack here, we'll crush every last one of them, so please don't worry. My comrades have all improved from training, and there are even masters like that Grand Hero stationed at the fortress. A bunch of Fiendbeasts won't be any trouble at all.

By the way, did you like the pastries I sent earlier? I didn't buy those—they were handmade by a cook girl I met here. Her name is Su Taotao, and she works as a skilled cook in the camp kitchen. She's kind, takes really good care of me, and her cooking is delicious. After spending so much time together and helping each other out, Taotao and I fell in love. She's completely sincere with me, and I feel the same way about her. Soon, I'm getting ready to tell her how I feel and ask her to spend her life with me. Once the war ends and the Fiend Tide recedes, I'm planning to bring her back home with me and open a pastry shop. I'll work the fields, and she'll run the kitchen. And you, Ma... you won't have to work at all. Just take it easy, enjoy your retirement, and get plenty of rest!

Please take good care of your health, Ma. And please give Taotao and me your blessing and grant this wish of mine. Wishing you good health, smooth sailing in all things, the blessing of lucky stars, freedom from illness and disaster, eternal youth and longevity, fulfillment of every heart's desire, wealth and prosperity, long life and vigor, peace of mind and body, endless good fortune, auspicious omens, every wish fulfilled, peace and safety, and a home brimming with good luck...

1518846:
"Chronicles of the Wandering Hero: Pompom"
In Jinghua Province, there lives a Pammy named Pompom, who has a passion for martial arts.

When asked about his hometown, he says Green Bamboo Ridge today, Scarlet Fruit Slope tomorrow, and Crouching Dragon Pool the day after.
When pressed further, he huffs in indignation: "A true master roaming the martial world does not lightly reveal the location of his family home!"
In the end, no one truly knows where Pompom came from.

Standing three feet tall, Pompom walks with his paws clasped behind his back, forever putting on the airs of a grandmaster.
He is especially fond of reading secret martial arts manuals—though, given how few characters he can actually read, what he pores over are mostly street picture books.
Once, people saw him holding a book and gazing at it in deep contemplation, thinking he had attained some profound enlightenment—until they stepped closer and saw he was holding it upside down.

Upon first visiting Jiyi Pavilion, Pompom was overjoyed, declaring that he had finally met his lifelong rival. He wrote a challenge letter in charcoal, stamped a paw print at the end, and solemnly slipped it into the mailbox by the gate.
After reading it, Quan folded it up and wedged it under a wobbly table leg.
Furious, Pompom began showing up at Jiyi Pavilion every single day from dawn till dusk, watching for a chance to duel.
Yet Quan treated him like a junior disciple and Peipei saw him as a playmate, so no matter how hard he provoked them, neither ever took him up on a fight.

Once, Pompom crouched in the corner by a wall, waiting for Peipei to walk past before leaping out with both paws raised high and roaring, "Raaah!"
When Peipei cheerfully replied, "Good morning," Pompom drooped in utter defeat.
Another time, he hid inside a cupboard, intending to jump out at midnight and frighten everyone.
When nobody could find him and they opened the cupboard, he was already fast asleep.

Though Pompom loves the martial way, everything he has learned is a chaotic hodgepodge.
He picks up three moves from street storytellers and steals five more from stage performances.
If he spots an escort martial artist on the road, he watches from afar for half a day and invents seven or eight fist styles of his own.
Thus, his techniques often boast thunderous names while achieving next to nothing.
His Soaring Dragon Cloud-Reaching Palm is really just reaching up to pick an Aple.
His Fierce Tiger Descending the Mountain Stance is simply slipping and tumbling down a slope.
As for his One-Legged Cabard Stance, nine times out of ten he just wobbles left and right.

Yet his luck is unmatched.
One day, overcome by hunger while trying to snatch some fruit, he accidentally startled a flock of birds. The birds taking flight spooked a wild boar, which bolted straight into a dead tree and snapped it in half.
When the tree toppled, a beehive tumbled out, treating Pompom to a feast of honey.
Whenever he tells this tale, Pompom never fails to beam with pride.

As the Starborn once remarked: "I have seen countless martial artists across the world. Some chase fame, some pursue fortune, and others fight out of fleeting pride.
Pompom's boxing is crude and his footwork clumsy, yet throughout his wanderings, he finds food when hungry, shelter when weary, and help whenever he stirs up trouble. Even in dire straits, he stumbles upon a way out by sheer fluke.
No matter the peril, he turns misfortune into blessing; no matter the obstacle, he blunders his way cleanly past it.
That, truly, is real kung fu."
1518847:
"A Wuxia Novel Written by Dingxiang for Peipei"
The wind sweeps through the bamboo grove, and the moonlight gleams like silver.
Secluded Bamboo Ridge lies cloaked in silence, with only two silhouettes standing face to face.
One stands with hands clasped behind his back, towering like a mountain—none other than Quan, the grandmaster whose name has resounded across Jinghua Province for decades.
The other wears a short martial tunic, holding both palms level before her with a solemn expression—none other than Peipei, the great Pammy hero whose fame has recently swept the martial world.
Their gazes meet. A brief moment passes.
Quan speaks first. "You've come."
Peipei nods. "Yes, I have."
Quan says, "You shouldn't have come."
Peipei replies, "Yet here I am."
Quan lets out a soft sigh. "In that case—"
Before the words have even faded, a sudden gale erupts!
Quan sweeps his sleeve, unleashing true qi from his entire body with a thunderous roar.
The bamboo grove sways and fallen leaves scatter wildly, as though ten thousand warhorses were thundering across the mountain.
Peipei steels her expression and plants her feet firmly upon the earth.
Her left palm moves like drifting clouds, her right like the moon, slowly unfolding the forms of the Pei-Style Fist and Palm.
Her palm strikes look gentle on the surface, yet as their force spreads, the swirling bamboo leaves freeze midair—as if time itself had slowed.
Quan's eyes brighten slightly in praise. "Fine palm technique!"
Stepping forward, he thrusts his right palm from within his sleeve. A plain, unadorned motion—yet it carries the crushing weight of a collapsing mountain.
Before the strike even arrives, the sheer wind pressure makes the surrounding bamboo and trees roar violently.
Unfazed, Peipei immediately circulates her true qi.
Crossing both palms, she conjures two faint currents of black and white qi.
The two forces collide with a deafening boom.
A dull shockwave echoes outward, shaking the mountain forest and sending countless birds fleeing into the sky.
When the dust settles moments later, neither has yielded a single step, standing right where they began.
Quan laughs heartily. "Good! Next move!"
With that, he leaps into the air and brings down a strike from the heavens.
Looking up, Peipei sees a palm force vast enough to blot out the sky and eclipse the moon, leaving nowhere to retreat.
In that hair's-breadth instant, a flash of inspiration strikes her. She closes her eyes, casts aside every martial form she has ever learned, and leaves only a single thought in her mind:
—If I can't win, I might as well take a nap first and think about it later.
In that instant, her mind clears completely, and yin-yang qi begins flowing effortlessly and endlessly throughout her body.
When she opens her eyes again, all of heaven and earth seems to move in slow motion.
Peipei calmly raises a hand and pushes forward—no form, no technique, no flash or artifice.
With a faint sound, the force of Quan's palm vanishes into nothing, and before anyone realizes it, Quan has drifted lightly back down to the ground.
Silence returns to the mountain valley.
After a long pause, Quan slowly asks, "What is the name of that technique?"
Peipei thinks for a moment, then answers honestly: "The Sleep-On-It Palm."
Quan falls deep into thought, and Peipei remains silent as well.
The night breeze blows past, rustling the bamboo leaves.
After a while, Quan nods quietly. "A fine name."
1518848:
Night's curtain falls, and all around grows still.
Starlight seeps into the lake, scattering points of gentle glow across the water. Moonlight ripples over the surface, stirring quiet waves within the girl's heart as well.
As she clasps her hands and softly chants a prayer, an old friend drifts lightly into view.
The figure appears cloaked in frost and snow, pure white yet tinged with a translucent azure hue. Eyes half-closed, it gently brushes its long snout against the girl's forehead.
"Tana," the girl smiles softly. "We meet again." As her fingertips touch her old friend's cheek, the Starborn hears the faint chime of a bell drifting through the air—so light and delicate, like an echo from beyond distant mountains. A breeze blowing out of the past ripples the water before them.
The girl feels her old friend's low hum, a sound brimming with deep peace stretching from afar. Through their shared memories, they reassure one another that their warmth has never been washed away by the years. Long ago, before she could summon spirits with prayers or read the revelations carried on the wind, whenever she sat hugging her knees in the quiet mountain wilds, there was always this same warm, snow-white silhouette beside her.
Something invisible slowly spreads between them—something that could only be called eternity, destined to be etched deeply into memory alongside that valley.
The wind dies down.
Time lingers within a clear, gentle azure glow as the silhouette of the girl and her old friend nestled close stands out against the boundless darkness of night.
"Did you see it?" the girl asks, opening her eyes and turning quietly toward the Starborn. "This is a miracle called back by the strength of our longing."
