1664488: Author's Note: "Cheshire Bat's Goodnight Fairytales" is a collection of stories that appeared around four hundred moons ago, and is said to have been burned as a banned book in a certain era. Therefore, only a few fragments have been passed down to posterity. The stories depicted within are an exaggerated interpretation of Kibo's actions in reality. Unlike intelligent races, Kibo should not excessively inject subjective speculation and imagination into research. However, the author believes that such works also possess existential value and can be collected as a literary genre. Therefore, I traveled across the continent, compiled them into a single volume, and republished them. Indeed, telling these as bedtime stories to children is not recommended, but interested Kibo researchers and story lovers will surely find other hypotheses and possibilities from them. I Became a Greaterg-- "Stuffing grain, stuffing grain, my belly is stuffed and making a ruckus. Schnellf comes and swallows me up, can't run away, can't hide." That was the fattest and plumpest Greaterg in the world. Its belly swelled up like a balloon, retreating to a place where it stayed completely motionless, unable even to roll over. It was extremely irritable, and if there was just a speck of dust on the grain, it would blow away all the grain just presented by the Grenards with an angry white snort. The poor Grenards had to gather clean grain all over again, and running around so frequently wore down their claws. Even so, the Greaterg was not satisfied, instructing the trembling Greenies with unopenable eyes to crawl underneath its bottom, and then crushing them down with all its might. Fearing its power and authority, the Greenies and Grenards served this fattest and plumpest Greaterg without rest. Because of this, everyone was emaciated, as thin as water-starved straw. I couldn't understand why everyone could accept such a life. I looked at the grain in my hand. This was food I had worked so hard to gather, so why couldn't I eat it and had to present it to that fat nuisance? I couldn't help asking the Greenies and Grenards nearby. "Why do we give our food to him?" Thy Greenies and Grenards looked at each other. "That's how we've always lived." "We are very weak, so we can't survive without relying on the Greaterg. He protects us." "In return, we should offer our food to him." They chirped one after another. "But he has never protected us even once! He's just taking away our grain..." Before I finished speaking, a terrifying howl could be heard from afar -- it was Schnellf! One, two... Schnellf's voices came from all directions, and we were surrounded! I led everyone running back to the Greaterg's territory, hoping to shake off these dangerous predators. But Schnellf pursued relentlessly, as if they had no intention of letting us go at all. More Greenies and Grenards joined our fleeing team, but the Greaterg stayed right where he was. Was he planning to act as the rearguard? Accompanied by the Greaterg's agonizing screams, Schnellf stopped chasing. The Greaterg's fat figure was blocked layer upon layer by the grass, getting smaller and smaller in our field of vision. It was obvious to everyone that he wouldn't survive. "Look, the Greaterg protected us," a Grenard said to me. The Greenies and Grenards looked very sad. A Greenie said, "I shed a single tear for the Greaterg." Another Greenie said, "As for me, I shed three tears." They surrounded me together. "Now that the Greaterg is gone, what should we do? You are the Grenard who led us to escape Schnellf's attack... Please, become our great king!" But I shook my head. "I don't want to become a Greaterg. I don't want to look as fat and lazy as that. Besides, the grain we gather should be shared equally among everyone." They did not reject my proposal, and together with me, built a new home in another wheat field. They listened to me very well. If I said a swing should be made of wheat leaves to the east, a swing was built in the east; if I said a grain storage room should be in the west, a large storage room was added in the west. Sometimes they would secretly hand over grain. At first, a Greenie secretly gave half of its grain, and I thought this was his goodwill and about half would be fine. But after that, even the Grenards started offering food, and unable to refuse, I had no choice but to eat that grain. After all, I am a Grenard, so I cannot resist the taste of grain. I gradually became lazy and grew fat. My tail dragged long behind me, and finally, I became the fattest and plumpest Greaterg. I became irritable, and my mind felt stuffed full of grain. I puffed out a white snort, and roared with my eyes: "Hand over the grain, hand over the grain! If you don't hand over the grain, I will put all of you under my bottom and crush you." Like my servants, they devoutly and respectfully offered every single harvested grain of wheat to me. And once again, the voice of Schnellf could be heard. One, two... They closed in on my territory. I wanted to run away quickly, but my body was too heavy, my head was heavy and could not be raised, and my limbs felt as if they were rooted in the ground. The Greenies and Grenards fled from my side at top speed, and only I couldn't move. Only one Greenie looked back at me once as he fled. He said to me -- "Dear Greaterg, I shed a single tear for you." (*There is a single line of annotation at the end: Perhaps what truly rules over them is the ears of golden wheat.)

1664490: Fleece Corner NewsNo. 034Chronicle Article: Today's Events at the Lord's ManorEarly in the morning, Fleece was enveloped in a pleasant tranquility. From the moment last night when my superior told me, "I want you to record Nanacha at the Lord's Manor," my heart soared high into the sky like a Mokyun, and my steps became light. And today, when I knocked on the door of the Lord's Manor, a sense of reality finally washed over me. Nanacha and Shine, the butler of the Lord's Manor, had already prepared warm tea. "You are our first guest today. The visitor from Elden Land is scheduled to arrive in an hour. Until then, please feel free to enjoy the tea pastries in the reception room." As expected of Head Maid Nanacha, her attentiveness and meticulous work ethic are bound to be praised by all visitors. It is said that Nanacha worked at the Lord's Manor even before the current lord took office. If she were to claim "I am second" in knowledge regarding the Lord's Manor, no one would dare claim first. That fact was strongly proven during this accompanying record as well. At 9:50 AM, ten minutes before the arrival of the next guest, Nanacha led the maids to tidy the carpet once more and arrange fresh tea pastries. The freshly brewed specialty scented tea was just at the right drinking temperature, the table was polished like new, and the sorted business documents were placed neatly in front of the lord's seat. Nanacha even paid attention to the changing light outside the window and adjusted the position of the curtains. "Count Bourgeois is very concerned about the ore procurement for the next quarter and related business partnerships, or rather, he feels quite anxious. I was hoping the aroma of scented tea and soft light could bring him a bit of ease," Nanacha explained. When the negotiations between the lord and Count Bourgeois began, Head Maid Nanacha waited in the lounge, keeping an eye out for anything needed in the reception room while helping Shine sort the letters that arrived from citizens last week. Among them were complaints regarding security and municipal issues, as well as gifts from residents. Nanacha explained it as follows: "The sheriffs and guards directly under the lord do their utmost to protect the citizens' lives. However, when you have suggestions regarding urban management or encounter difficult problems, you can also write a letter to consult the lord. The lord reads every single letter, because serving the people is our duty." In the afternoon, Nanacha helped process event applications submitted by various organizers and began cleaning the entire Lord's Manor. Tablecloths and cushions were sent to the laundry room, floor dust was wiped dry after cleaning, and all vase water was replaced. No matter how trivial the task, Nanacha never lost her gentle smile. "Making the mansion cleaner and ensuring everyone spends their time comfortably is my happiness." Night fell, and the day's work was coming to an end. Today's operations at the Lord's Manor were all finished, and my record was drawing to a close. Before seeing me off from the Lord's Manor, Nanacha handed me a gift she had prepared in advance. Kindness, professionalism, tolerance, sincerity... These were the deep charms I felt during my interactions with Nanacha that ordinary people simply do not possess. As expected of Pammy, who won first place in popularity as the "Fleece Ambassador Candidate"!
1664491:
"Let's go with this!"
In the sunlight, Amy raised her right hand high. Grasped in her hand was a large, plump, golden ear of wheat with full grains. Margaret nodded lightly and accepted the ear of wheat from Amy.
Amy stared at her sister's back. Due to days of continuous labor, that back seemed somewhat rounded. Her curly blonde hair was tied up roughly, shoved into a hood, and the dress she wore was patched in various places. A poignant ache welled up in her chest. Amy couldn't help but raise her voice.
-- Margaret, I'll help!
Margaret had already hung the golden ear of wheat on the house door. As the Golden Wheat Festival approached, every household was busy making preparations. This bundle of wheat Amy chose was much more beautiful than before, and she had a premonition that this moon would be a bountiful harvest moon.
Turning her back to Amy, she pointed toward the house.
"Go check on Lucy. She hasn't been feeling well this morning and has hardly eaten."
Amy turned around and entered the cabin.
Stepping on the wooden floor produced a nostalgic creaking sound. Amy had lived here all her life. Her family had lived in this house for generations. The cabin had undergone repeated repairs, and the timber making it up was probably completely different from a hundred moons ago. But the Wimbledon family was still here. The cupboard was filled with Caroline's small ceramic pieces. There were various works, such as farmers crouching to till the soil and Bangooses foraging in the wheat fields. Through Caroline's skilled hands, every single one of them seemed to breathe with life.
She looked at those small pieces and smiled. Amy had always believed in her sister's talent. If only Caroline had a single exhibition opportunity -- yes, just once -- then she would surely make a name for herself in Fleece. The only problem was where to find that opportunity.
"Big sister."
It was Lucy's voice. She quickly snapped out of her thoughts and headed toward the bedroom. Lucy was the youngest daughter of the Wimbledon family, quiet and introverted. She loved holding a pen by the window and writing things. However, she was not active and had a weak constitution. She often ran fevers or coughed. She didn't hear Lucy coughing, but Amy decided to bring her some warm tea.
"What's wrong, Lucy?"
Lucy directed her large, contemplative blue eyes toward her. Those eyes, which usually had a dreamy expression, now carried a slightly serious shade.
"I don't want to go to school anymore. My hair hurts so much."
she stated in a serious tone.
Amy blinked in confusion.
Hair? Perhaps it was a new excuse Lucy came up with to skip school, or perhaps Lucy was thinking about something else.

(Small handwritten pencil text under the manuscript paper) The four sisters of the Wimbledon family: Margaret, the steady and somewhat strict eldest sister; Amy, lively and resourceful; Caroline, the passionate artist; and Lucy, the shy and retiring youngest daughter who harbors literary dreams and always worries about family finances...
Ugh, one day, this story suddenly popped into my head. I should write it down... Maybe someone will publish it... No, my writing is still too immature, nobody would want to read it... But I want to write it...
1664492: Yester-tears and Tomorrows ThornsFour-Act Play: Serious Drama Characters Nikolai Andreyevich — Retired teacher. Igor Nikolayevich — His son, deceased. Elena Viktorovna — His son's wife, deceased. Sofia Igorevna — His granddaughter, a music conservatory student who dropped out of school. Act I Living room. An old wooden desk and two chairs are placed here. The candlelight glows dimly, and a faint fire burns in the fireplace. On the desk are a teacup, several sheets of paper, a quill, and an open ink bottle. In the corner, a Snowbow sleeps curled up. Nikolai, wearing glasses, sits facing the desk, flipping through a bundle of letters. Sofia paces back and forth across the room. Sofia Grandpa! Stop looking at those old letters! Ever since that day... since that day, has anyone ever sent us a single letter? Nikolai Memories of the past do not fade with time. Sofia (Laughing bitterly) Open your eyes and look! If you had any consideration at all, you'd notice the fire in the fireplace is about to go out. Don't you realize we are about to freeze to death?! Your old memories are only good for burning in the flames to keep warm! Nikolai Wait just a little longer. I want to keep these letters in my heart... Sofia Your students forgot about you long ago. Nikolai I remember every single one of them. Sofia Then do you remember? When your students signed that notice. Your son—my father—was killed in those disturbances. And yet, you still think of yourself as an old professor respected by your students? They killed our family, treated us like the ashes of burned-out firewood, and cast us into a corner of the world. If I could, I'd love to immerse myself in dreams of the past just like you. But to somehow maintain life in this tiny cabin, I have to keep my eyes wide open! Do you know how those people look at us? Pity mixed with contempt. They mouth platitudes about us being "unfortunate," but deep down they think we brought it on ourselves. Oh, if only we could vanish like April snow... where no one could see us... [Sofia stops, covers her face, and weeps.] Nikolai Sofia... That's a good girl, cry as much as you want. Sofia Why don't you ever cry? I've never seen you shed a single tear... Nikolai My tears dried up long ago. Come, take this, and let's give the past warmth one last time. [Sofia takes the bundle of letters from Nikolai's hands and tosses them into the fireplace. The flare burns brightly for an instant, then slowly dims once more.] Sofia And my sheet music... It's thick, so it can burn all night... Nikolai Keep the sheet music. Sofia It's fine, I've already memorized all of it. Nikolai Hold onto it. We will get through this. [The Snowbow in the corner wakes up and approaches Sofia.] Nikolai That's a good girl, sing me a song. Your singing always helps us forget our troubles. Sofia I haven't practiced singing in days. Nikolai Even so, your voice remains as beautiful as ever. [Sofia picks up the Snowbow and begins to hum softly. The Snowbow falls asleep.]
1664493:
A newly opened toy store on the busiest street in town had caught everyone's attention. Inside, a wide variety of plush toys, from giant bears to tiny rabbits, lined the shelves, each one looking utterly adorable. Hearing the rumors, Moflyne's curiosity was piqued once again.
Chirping happily with a "Nini~", it decided to sneak over and take a look inside the toy store.

"Mom, look! This plushie is so cute!"
"Dad! It feels great to hug, I want this one!"
Flying secretly into the toy store and seeing so many children happily hugging their plushies, Moflyne had a sudden inspiration—
"I'll become a plushie too, and let everyone hug me. It's bound to feel amazing!"
And so, using its magical power, Moflyne transformed into the appearance of a tiny child identical to a plush toy, blending right in among the stuffed animals.
Before long, several more children entered the toy store one after another. Everyone cheered, happily holding up cute plush toys, all eager to cuddle them.
When Moflyne, transformed into a plushie, was squeezed tightly by a child, it felt a warmth and comfort like never before. The sensation was so delightful that it couldn't help but purr!
"Huh? Why is this plushie purring?" the child asked in surprise.
The other children and adults in the store gathered around, staring curiously at the purring plush toy. Realizing its cover was blown, Moflyne shyly shifted back to its original form. Its eight ears swayed gently, and its eyes sparkled with a mischievous glint.
"Nini~" Moflyne greeted everyone in its unique voice, doing a joyful backflip in midair.
"Whoa! A flying plushie!"
"No way, isn't that a Kibo?"
"I've seen it in books! That's Moflyne! It's definitely Moflyne!"
The children cheered. They never imagined they would actually meet the legendary Moflyne! Ever since then, Moflyne stopped being a secret presence and became the biggest star in town.
And thanks to Moflyne's story, this toy store also became the children's favorite spot. Everyone knows that not only can you find cute plush toys there, but you might even encounter the real Moflyne. And from time to time, Moflyne returns to the toy store, transforms into a plushie, and enjoys the warmth of being cuddled.
Of course, by now it has learned how to control its purring and no longer gives away its identity so easily.

1664495:
Children, have you ever wondered why the wheat in Fleece is more golden than elsewhere, and why the river water is clearer and sweeter than the rest?
It is because, long, long ago, several gentle guardians lived right here.
And one of them was Amalthea. Her body was longer than ten Clodime connected end-to-end, her crown of horns was crystal clear, and her entire body was draped in stardust-like water light as she floated effortlessly in the air.
Amalthea is a Kibo that brought blessings to this land.
Back then, Fleece had just emerged from a massive war, and the earth was scorched black, with not even wild grass growing, let alone crops. Those who undertook the reclamation suffered from hunger while sowing seeds and watering them. Yet no one knew whether they would successfully harvest enough food in autumn to survive the winter.
Then, one such night, Amalthea arrived. No one saw where it came from. Some merely caught a glimpse of its glowing form far off under the moonlight. It stared at the cracked earth, stared at the dried-up riverbed, and shed a single tear.
Where that tear fell, the first post-war flower in Fleece blossomed.
From then on, the river water began to clear, the earth grew fertile, and the seeds they had sown sprouted firmly. Yet Amalthea did not leave, staying behind on a distant hill or lakeshore, watching quietly as they farmed, toiled, and built up Fleece step by step.
Today, Fleece grows more and more prosperous, with mills built and granaries established. But we must never forget that Amalthea once brought pure springs to Fleece and revived the vitality of this land...

"Dingxiang's Wuxia Novel Addressed to Peipei"
The wind blows through the bamboo grove, and the moonlight shines like silver.
Youhuang Ridge is shrouded in silence, with only two figures standing opposite each other.
One stands with hands clasped behind their back, towering like a mountain. That is none other than Quan, a grandmaster whose name has shaken Jinghua Cape for moons.
The other wears short garments, holding both palms horizontally with a solemn expression. That is none other than Peipei, a great martial hero of Pammy who has recently risen to fame in the Jianghu.
The two exchange glances. A moment passes.
Quan suddenly speaks up. "You've come."
Peipei nods. "Yes, I have."
Quan says. "You shouldn't have come."
Peipei replies. "But I am already here."
Quan sighs lightly. "In that case—"
Before the words could even finish, a fierce wind suddenly arose!
As Quan swings a sleeve, true qi is released from the entire body amidst a roaring sound.
The bamboo grove sways, fallen leaves scatter, resembling thousands of horses galloping across the mountains.
Peipei tightens expression, stamping firmly onto the ground.
The left palm like clouds, the right palm like moon. Slowly executing the forms of the "Pei Style Palm Arts".
The palm strike looks soft at first glance, but as the power reaches, the swirling bamboo leaves freeze mid-air, as if even time itself has slowed down.
Quan's eyes gleam slightly in praise. "Fine palm technique!"
Then taking a step forward, a right palm thrusts out from within the sleeve. It is a completely ordinary movement, yet it carries the oppressive force of a collapsing mountain.
Before the palm pressure even arrives, the surrounding bamboo and trees rattle violently from the wind pressure.
Peipei does not let down guard either, immediately circulating true qi.
Crossing both palms, faint wisps of black and white qi are generated.
The two forces collide with a deafening roar.
A muffled sound echoes, shaking the mountain forest and startling countless birds into flight.
After a moment, as the dust clears, the two stand right where they started, not yielding a single step.
Quan laughs heartily. "Good! Next!"
No sooner said than done, leaping up into the air, delivering a blow straight down from the heavens.
Peipei looks up, the force of that palm covering the heavens and hiding the moon. It feels as though there is nowhere left to retreat.
At that critical moment of crisis, inspiration strikes Peipei. Closing eyes, forgetting all previously learned techniques, leaving only a single thought in mind.
— If you can't win, you might as well take a nap and think about it later.
In that instant, the heart grows clear, yin and yang true qi circulate naturally, beginning to flow ceaselessly throughout the entire body.
Opening eyes once more, everything in heaven and earth seems to move in slow motion.
Peipei raises a hand calmly, pushing forward. No forms or techniques, no flashy maneuvers or skills.
A light sound rings out, and the force of Quan's palm vanishes instantly. Before anyone knows it, Quan descends gently and lightly onto the ground.
Silence returns to the mountain valleys.
After a brief silence, Quan speaks slowly. "What is the name of this technique?"
Peipei thinks for a moment, then answers honestly. "Sleeping Awakening Again Palm"
Quan ponders, and Peipei falls silent as well.
A night breeze sweeps through, rustling the bamboo leaves.
After a moment, Quan nods quietly. "A fine name."
1664498:
I always dream of that day.
There is no sound in the flames of the dream, and no temperature in the ruins. Only a suffocating mist rises from between the crumbled walls, swallowing everything familiar piece by piece.
So much time has passed since then. Yet the same sight returns before my eyes again and again, repeatedly reminding me—I couldn't protect the village. I couldn't protect everyone. Even continuing to live felt like a mistake I didn't know how to explain.

Perhaps that is why I was always afraid of drifting far away.
The inside of a coffin is narrow and dark. But it feels safer than the outside world. If I curl up inside, I don't have to think about terrifying things like "what should I do from now on."
As long as I guarded the buried memories, it felt like I could pretend time hadn't moved forward and retain this tiny comfort.

Lately, however, even that comfort is beginning to waver.
The dream grows more and more vivid, stirring up memories and rushing into my head all at once. Even sleeping felt like a punishment. I thought I just needed to endure a little longer. I was long used to it, and thought I could bear it alone.
And yet, Starborn-sama wore such a worried expression.
I tried to brush it off as usual, but those eyes couldn't be fooled. When looked at so earnestly, I felt like putting up a pretense was completely useless. That is why I followed Starborn-sama outside. To the sanatorium, to the mine. And most of all, to face the place I was most afraid of approaching once more.

The truth is, I was always afraid.
Of those memories, of the mist. Of being swallowed whole by the past if I stopped. What was even more terrifying was that my mission had ended, yet I was still lingering here. Not knowing where to go, or whether someone like me even had the qualification to move forward.
Sinking into a deep sleep and no longer thinking about anything might be much easier. If I just fall asleep like this, will I finally stop being afraid?

But Starborn-sama chased after me.
You told me you were worried. You told me there are still many beautiful things left in this world. You even said we could search for them together.

Yes, this life was preserved through everyone's blessings. It doesn't have to be solely for atonement, nor solely to guard ruins and mementos. It can also be to see different scenery and touch "the future" that I was too afraid to even imagine.

Starborn-sama, I am still scared.
Yet, if you are by my side. If those words were not just a passing whim. If you will reach out your hand just like today whenever I grow cowardly and stop in my tracks again—I think I want to try moving forward.
Even if it's just a single step, I want to walk into the world you speak of, where so many beautiful things exist.

I remember Peipei buying a few apples when they first appeared in the market. But shortly after walking a little ways, she hurried back, returned one of them to the storefront, and exchanged it for a smaller one.
I asked her, "What's wrong? Were those apples from earlier bruised?" She shook her head, hesitated for a moment, and said, "Everyone buys the big ones, so this small apple is going to be left unsold. It somehow feels a little pitiful..."
I almost burst out laughing. Then I gently patted the small apple in Peipei's hand and pushed the large apple she had just returned back against her chest. "You can have this one, too."
After thinking for a moment, I added, "I'm counting on you to take care of these little ones, you know! I've got the rest of the apples covered!"
Peipei nodded earnestly, and her expression was truly adorable.
——Greengrocer owner Massima

When Peipei comes to my shop, she usually doesn't buy anything. She doesn't seem interested in brightly polished gems; instead, she often lingers in front of the raw stones for a while.
Once, she stood staring intently at a batch of newly arrived unpolished stones. They hadn't been cut yet and looked quite plain.
When I asked her what she liked about them, she thought for a moment before answering slowly, "I don't know... but it somehow looks interesting."
I wanted to ask more, but she was already drawn away by the shouts of someone selling Peipei candy. Thanks to that, I ended up standing alone in front of the raw stones pondering for half a day. What on earth did Peipei find interesting about them?
——Gem shop owner Greidia

That day, I had just finished making a new batch of candy and wanted someone to taste-test it. Just as Peipei happened to walk past the front of the shop, I went out to greet her with the candy.
Thinking I was trying to make a sale, the child shook her head. I hurriedly explained that there was no money needed, it was just a free sample.
Peipei looked down at the candy, then looked at me, and finally asked in a small voice, "Since it's a tasting, does that mean I have to share my thoughts after eating it?"
Amused, I nodded.
At that, Peipei popped one of the candies into her mouth. She stood there chewing thoughtfully for a moment, then suddenly asked with a very serious look, "Grandpa Shine, if Peipei says it doesn't taste good, will you be sad?"
To be honest, I'm getting older and my sense of taste has faded a bit. It's true that sometimes new recipes I try don't turn out as expected.
However, everyone in town is a child whose growth I've watched over. To spare my feelings, they only ever offer praise. But when the new product actually launches, buyers are few and far between.
Peipei's words were a rare, genuinely sincere evaluation more precious than any empty flattery I had ever heard.
Afterward, I gifted Peipei a whole bag of candy as a thank-you. Naturally, it was our classic flavor, whose popularity had already been proven in the market.
——Candy shop owner Shine
